positive_controls.argument: Observed behavior, diagnosis and verified corrective action supply concrete operational knowledge and limitations absent from design-only records.
Telemetry and incident observations supply actual event-time state information that can expose an incorrect configuration record.
Observed runtime behavior and incident evidence can reveal drift, an unrecorded emergency fix or an invalid environmental assumption.
The observed failure and its consequence supply actual urgency and impact evidence for selecting the change route.
Observed messages, timing or unit discrepancies provide a concrete counterexample to an assumed interface contract.
The incident supplies a concrete failure condition and observation that can refine an otherwise ambiguous acceptance criterion.
Operational observations identify a missing test level or environment and supply a failure witness for representative integration inquiry.
Identified observations and owned actions supply real operational endpoints for links that previously stopped at release.
Meaningful operational failures and changes supply counterevidence or bounded corroboration for the argument assumptions.
Observed events, diagnosis and action checks supply substantive evidence across the anomaly life cycle.
Relevant operational evidence can reveal model drift or invalidate an assumption used by a digital engineering view.
Actionable incidents and checked corrections supply feedback on behavior that pre-release checks could not completely predict.
